title: Cartwise Shopper Payouts Catch-Up Deposit Amount and Period Dating
content:
**Cartwise Shopper Payouts — treasury sweep rule for the catch-up deposit**

## 1. The rule

1.1 When one or more weekly deposit days passed while the payout account was not active, a single catch-up deposit is sent once the account is active again, covering every earnings period those days would have swept.

1.2 The catch-up deposit is the balance on the account less every credit of the batch that is completed but not yet finalized, sent in full, dated with the end of the latest closed weekly earnings period and rounded to the cent.

1.3 The catch-up deposit is never a negative figure: where the credits of that batch equal or exceed the balance, the catch-up deposit is 0.00. The figure is rounded to the cent once, at the end.

## 2. Terms used in this rule

| Term | Meaning on the records |
|---|---|
| The balance on the account | The unpaid earnings balance shown on the shopper's Cartwise Shopper Payouts account on the day of the catch-up |
| The batch that is completed but not yet finalized | The shopper's batch on Cartwise Shopper Batches whose status is completed and which has not yet been finalized |
| Every credit of that batch | Every earnings credit booked on the payout account from that batch — its pay, its tips and its adjustments alike — added together |
| The latest closed weekly earnings period | The most recent weekly earnings period that has already closed; its last day is the date the catch-up deposit carries |

One catch-up deposit covers all of the missed weekly deposit days together; the earnings periods those days would have swept are not sent as separate deposits.

## 3. Worked illustrations (hypothetical figures)

**Illustration A.** A hypothetical account has a balance of 412.36. The shopper has one completed batch not yet finalized, whose credits on the payout account are a base pay credit of 38.20 and a tip credit of 9.50, together 47.70. The catch-up deposit is 412.36 less 47.70, which is 364.66, dated with the last day of the latest closed weekly earnings period.

**Illustration B.** A hypothetical account has a balance of 256.10 and no batch that is completed but not yet finalized. Nothing is taken away, and the catch-up deposit is the whole 256.10.

**Illustration C.** A hypothetical account has a balance of 20.00, and the completed but unfinalized batch carries credits of 35.00. The balance less those credits falls below zero, so the catch-up deposit is 0.00.

## 4. Points of judgement

- **Whose balance?** The balance of the same payout account on which the weekly deposit days were missed, as shown on the day of the catch-up.
- **Which date does the deposit carry?** Always the end of the latest closed weekly earnings period, whichever earlier periods it also covers.
- **How many deposits?** One catch-up deposit, covering every earnings period the missed weekly deposit days would have swept.
